title: Personal story about Google recruiter outreach
why: Personal recruiting anecdote with no technical lesson; the author notes it is not representative of Google.

title: Why companies hide blog post dates
why: Companies remove blog dates to hide inactivity, since stale posts make the site look stagnant; dated posts signal ongoing publishing.

title: Raw ApacheBench output comparing Go and Node
why: Pastes raw ApacheBench output from a local run with no analysis or method, so little standalone lesson is conveyed.

title: Argument that helmet promotion hurts cycling

title: How Geneva drives and heart cams work in watches
why: A trained watchmaker explains the Geneva drive smoothing mainspring power, heart cams resetting chronographs, and instantaneous date wheels.

title: Anecdote claiming psychosis is a metabolic fuel problem
why: Relies on personal anecdote and a contested metabolic theory of psychosis, with stated opinions that lack solid supporting evidence.

title: Speculative history of SubPop and Nirvana
why: Self-described rumor and conjecture about how SubPop released band demos as records; not reliable insider knowledge.

title: How foreigners' names are registered in Japan

title: Why datacenter-hosted darknet sites get found
why: Tor hides endpoint addresses but not traffic volume, so datacenter operators can spot high-bandwidth Tor servers and image them.

title: Venting about software career pressures
why: Emotional venting about work hours and career pressure compared with a welder; no technical lesson for readers.

title: Why semantic versioning compresses too much meaning
why: Argues SemVer reduces breaking-change severity and user impact to one number, making version numbers less informative to humans than before.

title: Lonely sysadmin venting about small-company IT
why: Venting about being the only tech person at a small firm; mostly personal complaint without a transferable lesson.

title: Perspective on Aaron Swartz sentencing
why: Opinion about sentencing and civil disobedience in the US, contested legal argument rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Residual stream keeps consistent representations across layers

title: How Guake began as a GTK Yakuake alternative
why: Original author explains that Guake was built as a GTK drop-down terminal because Yakuake required Qt, with early design choices.

title: Argument that IP laws do not block innovation

title: Rant about Argentine government corruption
why: Political rant about corruption and vote-buying in Argentina and the US, without concrete evidence or technical content.

title: Why the AWS console gets less design investment

title: Rant about Match, Epic and Spotify

title: Disparate impact: discrimination without intent

title: Speculative pharmacology questions about bromantane
why: Speculative pharmacology musings and open questions about dopamine and serotonin effects, with claimed expertise but no firm conclusions.

title: Monitoring a page for changes to catch openings
why: Practical method: diff a web page every 10 minutes for a keyword and trigger Twilio alerts, to catch brief application windows.

title: Personal reflection on family and moving home
why: Personal reflection about family ties and whether to move back to New Orleans; no lesson for a technical reader.

title: Personal account of a child services investigation
why: Personal account of being investigated after helping a friend's family; emotional narrative with no transferable lesson.

title: Defends India as a place for startups

title: Why Bakken gas lacks pipelines and markets
why: Pipeline buildout lags Bakken drilling, so oil moves by truck and associated gas lacks buyers, while low US gas prices slow investment.

title: Argument for mitigation over containment in COVID
why: Policy argument favoring mitigation over lockdown, mixing opinion with serology claims and calling opponents names; contested rather than explanatory.

title: Rant that science was defunded for political reasons
why: Partisan political argument about science funding; lists funders of basic research but mainly polemic.

title: Argument that cattle methane is not new
why: Argument comparing cattle herd size to historical bison populations; rhetorical comparison, not a rigorous emissions analysis.

title: Film resolution and CG adoption history
why: Early films on 16mm or 35mm were sharp enough for HD; sound spread within three years under commercial pressure, a precedent for tech shifts.

title: Common misreadings of heritability in intelligence research
why: Corrects common misunderstandings of heritability for human intelligence and points to behavioral genetics literature as the place to learn current research.

title: Newcomer's view on HN community quality
why: Newcomer's reflections on online community discussion quality and whether to participate; opinion without a technical lesson.

title: Quotes on Platonism and mathematical truth
why: Mostly quotes an article on Platonism and mathematics with brief commentary; discussion of views rather than a clear explanation.

title: Java vs Scala performance and tech politics
why: Opinion about performance FUD and politics in tech disputes; the claim that code quality matters more than language is arguable.

title: Why hospital computerization clashes with clinical culture
why: ER nurse explains how medicine's slow, safety-first change culture clashes with fast IT cycles, so computerized workflows can add risk.

title: Defense of Dubai against critics
why: Opinion defending Dubai and mocking critics, with political comparisons and no substantive analysis of governance.

title: Why bug bounties lose to black-market exploit prices
why: Bounties work only if payouts are worth a finder's time yet well below criminal buyers' prices; otherwise bugs get sold instead of reported.

title: Fantasy of living permanently in a hotel
why: Personal lifestyle fantasy about outsourcing home chores to a hotel; no technical or factual lesson.

title: Linux desktop gaps versus macOS for a switcher
why: X11 struggles with multi-monitor tearing and mixed DPI, Wayland is still rough, and macOS Preview and gestures lack Linux equivalents.

title: Hiring manager's case for simple SQL screening
why: Hiring manager says a basic job-relevant SQL test filters out candidates who overstate skills; good candidates finish it in about two minutes.

title: Why E Ink displays stay expensive
why: Visionect founder explains E Ink and driver costs are high at low volume; office signage and solar bus stops are the likely growth markets.

title: Complaint about fragmented math education
why: Personal frustration about UK maths curriculum and missing topics; argues for a map of fields, but largely reflective opinion.

title: Practical B2B SaaS pricing: price higher, tier three plans
why: Price above comfort; a three-tier $49/$99/$249 default; avoid clients under $29 a month, who churn and consume support time.

title: Personal review of a small Palm phone
why: Personal device review praising size and fewer notifications; a product opinion rather than a transferable technical lesson.

title: Network simplex keeps integer solutions for flow problems
why: With integer arc capacities and a feasible bounded problem, network simplex keeps integer solutions and solves many matching problems efficiently.

title: Why IoT devices get tethered to vendor clouds
why: Vendors tether devices to clouds for lock-in and secrecy against cheap rivals, while messy endpoint networks make direct end-to-end transit hard to build.

title: Interviewing by discussing past projects, not whiteboards
why: Read resumes closely, then discuss projects in depth: what was enjoyable, hardest, and what would change, with no whiteboard coding or trivia.

title: Argument about copyright on space footage
why: Argues NASA footage was free to use while SpaceX footage is copyrighted; a policy opinion with contested claims about usage.

title: Struggling to find startup ideas
why: Personal account of failing to find startup ideas and regulatory obstacles; reflective, with no general lesson beyond frustration.

title: Why lab replications fail: unwritten experimental conditions
why: Methods sections omit tacit controls like noise, cage cleanliness and handling; failed replications often reflect unrecorded variables, not falsity.

title: Personal reflection on generalist career path
why: Personal career reflection about switching roles and worries about specialization; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Critique of a letter about App Review
why: Critiques a letter's tone and motives and speculates about the author's business; argument about Apple rather than explanation.

title: Argument about Jack Ma's disappearance

title: Personal bed bug infestation story
why: Personal bed bug story describing itch and allergic welts; mainly anecdote, with the Morgellons link left unclear.

title: Claims about grid capacity for EVs
why: Unverified self-built fleet model claiming 900 to 1400 GW needed; assumptions are not laid out, so the number cannot be checked.

title: Why clients must store reversible saved passwords
why: Clients must replay plaintext or reversible credentials, so hashing is impossible; a hard-coded key is weak but beats plaintext, and DPAPI is better.

title: First impressions of the Yahoo homepage
why: Subjective design critique of Yahoo's homepage, covering the prompt, jingle, and search bar; opinion without technical depth.

title: Practical notes on returning to college as an adult
why: Community colleges often have strong professors and treat adults as adults; universities are slower and more distracting, so starting at community college can work well.

title: Worry about losing ownership to subscriptions
why: Opinion essay worrying that subscriptions erode ownership of books and music; concern without concrete mechanism or analysis.

title: Personal reflection on undiagnosed autism
why: Personal account of growing up undiagnosed and learning social skills; moving but anecdotal, without a transferable technical or factual lesson.

title: How NTIA facial recognition guidelines actually work
why: NTIA process covers only voluntary commercial guidelines, excluding government use; companies that break their own published policies face FTC sanctions.

title: Why TARP and QE differ in government accounting
why: TARP ran through Treasury and profited; QE was Federal Reserve asset purchases, with profits remitted to Treasury by statute.

title: Moderator note on flagged Uber stories
why: Moderator note about flagging decisions on Uber stories and how URLs get chosen; site-governance content, not a technical lesson.

title: Claim that microservices are developer fiefdoms
why: Cynical claim that microservices serve team territory rather than engineering goals; opinion rather than evidence or explanation.

title: Tom Wheeler's cable trade association years
why: Wheeler headed the cable trade association, not one company, from 1976 to 1984; the tech press oversimplified his lobbying background.

title: Live notes on Alphabet's quarterly earnings
why: Live investor notes on quarterly numbers, analyst ratings and trading moves; market commentary without durable technical knowledge.

title: Analogy: programming as music, not engineering
why: Analogy comparing programming to music and claiming it is easier than engineering; persuasive framing with no concrete evidence.

title: Allegations linking NordVPN and ProtonVPN to Tesonet
why: Allegations about corporate ties and a removed About page, with partisan framing and limited verifiable detail.

title: Mapping where 2008 tech startups were acquired
why: Lists where 2008 acquired startups were based and notes most were outside the Valley; raw data without analysis or method.

title: How DVD region encryption sparked Linux DeCSS

title: State versus nation in post-colonial Africa
why: Argues post-colonial states failed because borders ignore nations, a contested political thesis presented without evidence or counterexamples.

why: Markdeep puts Markdown in the body, so browsers parse text like '<string' as HTML; TeXMe's textarea keeps input intact and parses more robustly.

title: Forum policy on political posts

title: Opinion on replacing laptops with a phone

title: Timing gcc and clang preprocessing on Boost
why: Reply with raw preprocessing timings for gcc and clang on Boost headers; too context-dependent to teach a standalone lesson.

title: Personal gripes about Facebook social pressure
why: Personal complaints about professional contacts, reputation and social pressure on Facebook; anecdotal venting without a general lesson.

title: Rant about Levandowski's pay and trade secrets
why: Moralizing rant about executive pay and a trade-secret case, with speculation about motives and no technical substance.

title: Argument that Sparta achieved nothing
why: Polemic comparing Sparta unfavorably with Mongols and Romans; opinion-driven with contested historical judgments.

title: Rebuttal of GNU's Google privacy report
why: Argues GNU exaggerates normal Android features like malware removal and parental controls; a debate over framing rather than explanation.

title: Essay blaming individualism for family decline
why: Opinion essay about individualism, careers and family life, drawn from personal observation rather than evidence.

title: Argument for moderating hate speech on 8chan
why: Political argument about free speech and hate moderation, invoking Popper; contested opinion rather than explanatory knowledge.

title: Wishlist for cleaning up the Java standard library
why: Opinion wishlist for Java cleanup and a regex literal, with general comments about the JVM and no deep technical explanation.

title: Personal COVID rapid test false negatives

title: Simple bearer tokens beat JWTs for most APIs

title: Argument that app store fees need no justification
